- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.80) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% in subsequent periods.
- After a sharp price spike (≥10% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +5% above immediate prior high.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.20) mid-period, model fails to adjust downward; apply downward bias of 2–5% per negative sentiment day.
- Model underestimates mean-reverting trends when sentiment is neutral (0.20–0.50); add 1–3% upward bias to forecast if sentiment remains flat for 3+ days.
- For 30-day forecasts, model consistently overestimates early days (1–7) when sentiment is volatile; reduce first 3 forecast points by 3–7% if sentiment swings >0.30.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion within 10 days, model overreacts; apply 2–5% downward correction to forecast 10–15 days ahead if sentiment is weak or flat.
